name_story.story: Uzma can be understood through the Arabic form عُظْمَى, whose central sense is uzma; greatest, supreme (feminine). Uzma is Arabic عُظْمَى (ʿUẓmā), the feminine elative of عَظِيم, meaning 'greatest, supreme'.

faq.a: Uzma is associated with the Arabic form عُظْمَى, whose core sense is uzma; greatest, supreme (feminine).

faq.q: What is the origin of Uzma?
faq.a: Uzma is associated with Arabic. Uzma is Arabic عُظْمَى (ʿUẓmā), the feminine elative of عَظِيم, meaning 'greatest, supreme'.
Yes — the underlying form عُظْمَى is Arabic.
Uzma can occur in Muslim naming contexts, but it is better described as a Arabic-origin name used within some Muslim naming traditions than as an exclusively Islamic religious term.
Uzma should not be classified as a Quranic personal name without a direct Quranic basis. The root ع ظ م is Quranic (greatness), but ʿUẓmā is not itself a Quranic personal name.

faq.q: What does Uzma mean in Urdu?
faq.a: In Urdu, Uzma is rendered عظمیٰ and carries the sense عظمیٰ، سب سے بڑی.

faq.q: What does Uzma mean in Persian?
faq.a: In Persian, Uzma is rendered عظمی and carries the sense عظمی، بزرگ‌ترین.
A romanized syllable approximation is uz-ma. No IPA transcription is asserted because a verified phonetic transcription was not available.

faq.q: What are the variants of Uzma?
faq.a: Romanization variants include Uzma, uzma. Script forms are عظمی, عظمیٰ, عُظْمَى, उज़्मा.

faq.q: Is Uzma a boy's or girl's name?
faq.a: Documented usage records this form as female. Gender is not inferred from the meaning of the word, and actual use may vary between communities.
